attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed open letter.

semantics.note: 'Much worse' is a fair paraphrase of 'not nearly as good'. It is a comparative observation about deep learning as of May 2022.

contract.note: Marcus gave no measure and no size of gap. The contract fairly asks for a common comparison standard, but the result depends on that choice.

evidence.note: CoCa (May 2022) shows strong image classification. That backs the object-recognition half but gives no common scale for comparison.
A January 2022 paper finds both useful zero-shot planning and limits on executability. It has no comparison with recognition.
PaLM (April 2022) reports strong language results, some above average human performance, which cuts against the claim. Still, it gives no common-scale comparison.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows strong object recognition, mixed planning results and strong language benchmarks (PaLM). None of it puts the abilities on the common standard the contract requires, and the packet says so. It does not settle whether planning, reading and comprehension were 'not nearly as good'.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in the signed letter. It was adapted from work with Davis, but he states it in his own voice.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will not' with the horizon 'In 2029'. The proposition keeps the scope ('arbitrary', 'from the mathematical literature', 'symbolic form').

contract.note: Setting the deadline at the end of 2029 and reading 'arbitrary' as broad and independently selected is fair. The early-resolution rule sensibly needs broad, faithful, reproducible conversion.

evidence.note: M2F (February 2026) formalized two selected analysis textbooks. That is real progress, but it does not show faithful conversion of arbitrary literature proofs.
Anthropic's own announcement (September 2026) reports a checked Lean proof of Fermat's Last Theorem. It is a company disclosure about one selected project and does not show arbitrary-proof breadth.
Meta's own announcement (October 2026) of AutoformBench. In it, humans formalized the target statements, so it does not show full conversion of arbitrary proofs.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2029) is after the evaluation date. The advances in the packet are selected projects or partly human-assisted benchmarks. None of them is independently reproduced broad, faithful conversion of arbitrary literature proofs, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed open letter.

semantics.note: 'Unsolved' slightly flattens 'remains a challenge', but it is faithful to the overall statement about the state of things in 2022.

contract.note: Reading the claim as material remaining limitations, not a total absence of progress, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: ModelNet40-C (January 2022) finds a significant robustness gap in state-of-the-art 3D point-cloud recognition.
The May 2022 ScanQA revision finds object identification still a bottleneck for 3D scene question answering, and it reports modest scores.

reviews.rationale: Studies from before May 31, 2022 show significant robustness gaps in 3D perception and remaining bottlenecks in 3D scene understanding. The packet has nothing showing broadly reliable solutions in either area.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed open letter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the comparative 'more on big data than on reasoning' and correctly takes the issue to be long-tail rare events, as the context shows.

contract.note: Reading 'very serious' as substantial reliability limits, not an impossibility claim, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: A survey released May 27, 2022 finds that conventional deep learning performs poorly on rare (tail) classes.
PaCo (2021) shows long-tail mitigation methods were improving. That qualifies the claim but does not show the problem was solved.

reviews.rationale: The research synthesis from just before the post documents poor rare-class performance in mainstream deep learning. The mitigation work shows progress, not a solution. The evidence is mostly about vision, but it fits the contract's reading.
